raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary (human-written)

<!-- author fills in -->

## Problem

`MuseGlimmerStateDictAdapter` permutes q/k rows between torchtitan's interleaved and HF's split-half RoPE layouts. The k call sites in `to_hf` and `from_hf` pass the projection's `(head_dim * n_kv_heads, dim)` explicitly, so a tensor with the projection's rows but another second dim fails in the `view`. Concrete case: exporting a rank-r LoRA factor `lora_B` of the fused `wqkv` through `to_hf` (as an RL trainer does to serve the adapter) raises

```
RuntimeError: shape '[2, 32, 2, 256]' is invalid for input of size 512
```

on the `debugmodel` flavor with a rank-4 factor. The q path already sized itself from the tensor.

## Change

The permute only reorders rows, so `_permute` and `_reverse_permute` take `(rows, cols)` from the tensor, the `dim1`/`dim2` parameters go away, and the geometry helper returns only the head counts that remain in use. No numerics change for weights: the explicit dims equaled the weight's own shape.

## Testing

- New CPU unit test `TestMuseGlimmerStateDictAdapterRowPermute`: a rank-wide factor exports with the q/k/v row counts and the same row order as the weight. Fails on main with the error above, passes with the change.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_glimmer/test_muse_glimmer.py`: 6 passed.
- Loading `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` and exporting it back through `to_hf` is bit-exact against the safetensors (TP=1 and TP=2) before and after.

<!-- ciflow-pending -->
~~Workflows were awaiting approval.~~ CI has now been triggered for the ciflow labels on this PR.

**Claude finished @felipemello1's task in 2m 13s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41360946635)

---
**Approve -- please address the items before merging** (empty human-written summary; new test class sits after `unittest.main()`). See the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5726#pullrequestreview).
@HJSang please fix lint error, and any other after CI check is over

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The fix deletes dead size parameters, so the row permute sizes itself from the tensor. Weights get the same result as before, and the change touches only the muse_glimmer adapter. A maintainer still needs to review.

**What this PR does.** `_permute` / `_reverse_permute` used to accept optional `dim1`/`dim2`. Only the text k-projection call sites passed them, always as `(head_dim * n_kv_heads, dim)`, which for a real `wk` equals `w.shape`. The PR drops those parameters, reads `(rows, cols)` from the tensor, and shrinks `_attn_geometry` to `_attn_heads`, since `dim` and `head_dim` no longer have a consumer.

**Example.** On the `debugmodel` flavor, a rank-4 factor with the fused `wqkv` row count goes through `to_hf`:
```
before: _permute(wk_factor, n_kv_heads, head_dim*n_kv_heads, dim)
        -> view(2, 32, 2, 256) on a (128, 4) tensor -> RuntimeError
after:  _permute(wk_factor, n_kv_heads)
        -> view(2, 32, 2, 4) -> (128, 4), rows in the same order as the weight
real wk (128, 256): identical in both versions (explicit dims == w.shape)
```

### Must fix
1. PR description -- the "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author needs to fill it in (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`, "AI-assisted contributions").
2. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_glimmer/test_muse_glimmer.py:158` -- the new test class sits after `unittest.main()`, so it doesn't run when the file is executed directly. Move it above the `__main__` block.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/models/muse_glimmer/state_dict_adapter.py:149` -- llama3 has the identical `dim1/dim2` permute and explicit k call sites with the same failure. Apply the same deletion there, or say why not.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_glimmer/test_muse_glimmer.py:164` -- use the adapter class directly instead of `type(config)._owner`. Also reconsider whether the test earns its place: it guards a loud failure for an out-of-repo caller.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Gate.** The failure is real on `main`: a non-weight tensor with q/k rows can't be exported. No in-repo path sends a LoRA factor through `to_hf`. `torch_checkpointing.py` exports model weights, and the RL vLLM wrapper loads weights. So the motivating caller is out-of-repo. The change is still a net deletion that removes parameters only one call site used, which passes the minimalism bar without needing a consumer.
- **DTensor / TP.** `dtensor_safe` (`torchtitan/models/base/state_dict_adapter.py:29`) redistributes to Replicate before calling the permute. `w.shape` is therefore the global shape under FSDP/TP, the same value the explicit dims carried before.
- **Numerics.** No change for weights, because the removed arguments equaled `w.shape` at every call site. The description's bit-exact 30B export at TP=1/2 is consistent with this.
- **Prior art.** `muse_spark/state_dict_adapter.py:39` (`_permute_rope_rows`) already sizes its permute from the tensor. That helper is private to muse_spark, so not reusing it here is correct.
</details>

Not verified: I could not run the unit tests in this environment.

This class is defined after `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()`. `unittest.main()` calls `sys.exit`, so running the file directly (`python test_muse_glimmer.py`) never defines this class and the test silently doesn't run. pytest still collects it. Move the class above the `__main__` block.

`type(config)._owner` reaches into a private attribute of the config machinery. Import `MuseGlimmerStateDictAdapter` from `torchtitan.models.muse_glimmer.state_dict_adapter` and call `MuseGlimmerStateDictAdapter(config, None)` directly.

Also consider whether this test is worth keeping at all (`rules/tests.md`). The regression it guards fails loudly (a `RuntimeError` in `view`), and nothing in the repo exports a LoRA factor through `to_hf`. Row-order correctness for real weights is already covered by the HF numerics check. If a maintainer wants the guard, keeping it is fine. Otherwise, deleting it keeps this PR a pure net deletion.

+        """The q/k RoPE permute reorders rows only, so a LoRA factor with the projection's rows
+        and a rank-wide second dim must follow the weight's row order; sizing the k permute from

+        rows = (attention.n_heads + 2 * attention.n_kv_heads) * attention.head_dim

+            torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.float32)[:, None]
+            .expand(rows, rank)
+            .contiguous()
+        )
+        weight = (
+            torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.float32)[:, None]
+            .expand(rows, config.dim)
+            .contiguous()
+        )
+
+        exported = adapter.to_hf({"layers.0.attention.qkv_linear.wqkv.weight": factor})
+        reference = adapter.to_hf({"layers.0.attention.qkv_linear.wqkv.weight": weight})
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {name: tuple(tensor.shape) for name, tensor in exported.items()},
+            {
+                f"model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn.{proj}.weight": (out, rank)
+                for proj, out in (
+                    ("q_proj", attention.n_heads * attention.head_dim),
+                    ("k_proj", attention.n_kv_heads * attention.head_dim),
+                    ("v_proj", attention.n_kv_heads * attention.head_dim),
+                )
+            },
+        )
+        for name, tensor in exported.items():
+            torch.testing.assert_close(tensor[:, 0], reference[name][:, 0])
+
+

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The fix deletes dead size parameters, so the row permute sizes itself from the tensor. Weights get the same result as before, and the change touches only the muse_glimmer adapter. A maintainer still needs to review.

**What this PR does.** `_permute` / `_reverse_permute` used to accept optional `dim1`/`dim2`. Only the text k-projection call sites passed them, always as `(head_dim * n_kv_heads, dim)`, which for a real `wk` equals `w.shape`. The PR drops those parameters, reads `(rows, cols)` from the tensor, and shrinks `_attn_geometry` to `_attn_heads`, since `dim` and `head_dim` no longer have a consumer.

**Example.** On the `debugmodel` flavor, a rank-4 factor with the fused `wqkv` row count goes through `to_hf`:
```
before: _permute(wk_factor, n_kv_heads, head_dim*n_kv_heads, dim)
        -> view(2, 32, 2, 256) on a (128, 4) tensor -> RuntimeError
after:  _permute(wk_factor, n_kv_heads)
        -> view(2, 32, 2, 4) -> (128, 4), rows in the same order as the weight
real wk (128, 256): identical in both versions (explicit dims == w.shape)
```

### Must fix
1. PR description -- the "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author needs to fill it in (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`, "AI-assisted contributions").
2. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_glimmer/test_muse_glimmer.py:158` -- the new test class sits after `unittest.main()`, so it doesn't run when the file is executed directly. Move it above the `__main__` block.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/models/muse_glimmer/state_dict_adapter.py:149` -- llama3 has the identical `dim1/dim2` permute and explicit k call sites with the same failure. Apply the same deletion there, or say why not.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/muse_glimmer/test_muse_glimmer.py:164` -- use the adapter class directly instead of `type(config)._owner`. Also reconsider whether the test earns its place: it guards a loud failure for an out-of-repo caller.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Gate.** The failure is real on `main`: a non-weight tensor with q/k rows can't be exported. No in-repo path sends a LoRA factor through `to_hf`. `torch_checkpointing.py` exports model weights, and the RL vLLM wrapper loads weights. So the motivating caller is out-of-repo. The change is still a net deletion that removes parameters only one call site used, which passes the minimalism bar without needing a consumer.
- **DTensor / TP.** `dtensor_safe` (`torchtitan/models/base/state_dict_adapter.py:29`) redistributes to Replicate before calling the permute. `w.shape` is therefore the global shape under FSDP/TP, the same value the explicit dims carried before.
- **Numerics.** No change for weights, because the removed arguments equaled `w.shape` at every call site. The description's bit-exact 30B export at TP=1/2 is consistent with this.
- **Prior art.** `muse_spark/state_dict_adapter.py:39` (`_permute_rope_rows`) already sizes its permute from the tensor. That helper is private to muse_spark, so not reusing it here is correct.
</details>
